workstation_lifecycle_bootstrap_repair.authority_separation: A signed-in developer on a durably trusted Full Harness device may now launch the exact room/environment workstation lifecycle with action_authority_id null. The trust UI explicitly discloses installed local environment application start/stop authority while withholding in-environment Minecraft action, World Authority, answer authority, and terminal authority.
workstation_lifecycle_bootstrap_repair.replacement_boundary: restart_client=true still requires an exact active Player Embodiment authority.
workstation_lifecycle_bootstrap_repair.full_typescript_check_detail: A 7 GiB checkout-wide tsc run completed without an out-of-memory failure and emitted the repository's existing broad type-error baseline across unrelated CLI, document-viewer, Helix legacy-test, and physics files. No captured diagnostic named a file changed by this repair. The piped shell exit was not used as a success verdict; focused compile-through tests are the gate for this patch.

post_lifecycle_capacity_instrumentation_.reporter_repair: A latency family is now missing only when every sample is null. Zero raw-event coverage and zero model/tool round trips are separately reported as observation:coalescing and progress:model_tool_round_trip gaps.

onboarding_product_findings.recommended_primary_surface: A launcher-style environment workflow catalog with one large Play Minecraft with Helix tile. The tile composes readiness checks, exact-task selection, trusted local lifecycle, connector rotation, subject selection, finite action authority, fresh perception, and steering readiness behind one visible state machine.
onboarding_product_findings.settings_presentation: Detailed identity, authority, pairing, and diagnostic controls remain available as an advanced drill-down rather than the primary start path.
onboarding_product_findings.durable_state_boundary: Account session, installed-device trust, chosen workflow, environment profile, and operator-visible connection alias may persist. Connector credentials and in-environment action authority remain finite, revocable, scope-bounded, and truthfully renewed or re-requested; Start is not unlimited ambient authority.
onboarding_product_findings.authentication_expectation: A valid native account session should normally survive ordinary EXE reopen. Interactive authentication is required only when the account session is absent, expired, revoked, or policy requires reauthentication.
onboarding_product_findings.current_stopped_task_behavior: A finalized typed or GPT Live steering event is retained in the exact server-side binding mailbox until its event expiry, but a stopped Codex task does not poll, acknowledge, or reason over it. A later manually resumed turn may read it if still valid.
onboarding_product_findings.provider_wake_requirement: A real wake requires a provider-supported continuation or task-message transport plus explicit user authorization and exact task identity. MCP polling, UI automation, fabricated provider tasks, and steering receipts cannot substitute for that transport.
onboarding_product_findings.binding_label_gap: The current UI exposes opaque binding and continuation identifiers but has no provider task title. The product should display a user-owned connection alias composed from the workflow and Helix chat title while keeping opaque IDs in diagnostics; it must not claim a Codex task title the provider did not supply.

negative_evidence.detail: After exact task binding, the MCP environment directory truthfully listed the installed Minecraft Fabric environment but reported every retained connector epoch offline or missing. The newest retained binding had an expired credential and stale contact, so no fresh subject or observation was available. A new Player Embodiment authority could not be configured against that stale identity, returning a retryable internal error. This confirms the user-facing order must be exact task binding -> environment selection -> trusted local lifecycle start -> fresh connector/subject verification -> finite action authority -> steering, rather than asking for a gameplay prompt immediately.

The MCP-only self-repair attempt refreshed exact local-supervisor presence, but the transition request reused a prior transition_accepted record whose original delegation could not authorize a new execution idempotency key. The tool-list-changed notification was emitted, yet the running Codex catalog retained the old lifecycle input schema. No reconnect, environment authority, or gameplay action was falsely claimed.

The native pairing handoff targeted the keyed EXE's configured combat-c0-server profile while a generic documented bootstrap initially launched the parent run directory. The wrong-profile server rejected the unrelated credential and was stopped through Minecraft's normal stop command before the exact profile was launched.

The exact-profile server rejected the first staged handoff as server_pairing_inbox_stale after diagnosis exceeded the inbox window. A freshly issued rotation was redeemed immediately and manifest admission succeeded.

The MCP client lifecycle requires an active Player Embodiment authority, but a new authority requires a fresh online player subject that is unavailable until the client joins. The existing broker script was invoked only to bootstrap client presence; it granted no environment authority.

The first post-cycle-3 read-only perception request remained live for about 105 seconds and completed with an empty wrapper rather than a typed observation or typed failure. A later fresh probe succeeded; no action was replayed while the first outcome was unknown.

After the operator reported sending the requested natural prompt in the packaged EXE, three exact binding reads after cursor 0 remained empty. No pickup or acknowledgement was claimed. The composer defaults to the Helix Ask destination rather than the active bound-agent destination, and the current MCP catalog exposes claim/read/acknowledge but no operator-message submission tool.
negative_evidence.resolution: The operator selected Bound external AI task once; the next normal prompt arrived as exact steering cursor 1 and was acknowledged. Source now auto-selects the active exact binding until an operator explicitly chooses another destination.

negative_evidence.detail: The player-pair MCP input calls its target binding_id while the action authority is keyed by environment_binding_id. Passing the environment binding produced connector_pairing_not_found; the required value was the room_source_binding_id. The error failed closed and no credential was exposed.

The operator sent Helix steering while the exact Codex task was stopped. The event could remain pending in the bounded server-side store, but no provider-supported transport woke the task. Pickup occurred only after the Codex task resumed and explicitly read the mailbox. The UI must distinguish queued for pickup from task awakened.

The exact cryptographic binding and continuation references prove machine identity but are unsuitable as the primary user label. Current presence publishes no provider task title, so the UI needs a user-owned alias and Helix-chat/workflow labels without inventing provider metadata.

A local process-identity diagnostic revealed that the official Minecraft launcher includes a session credential in the Java client command line. The credential value is intentionally omitted from this evidence. Future process diagnostics must select or redact command-line fields rather than emitting the raw command line.

A reused accepted transition request reported reconnect_required=true and catalog_refresh_required=true despite the already-active stable-scope router. This contradictory nonterminal receipt could send an agent and user into an unnecessary restart loop; source defaults and focused coverage were repaired.

Review found that a native non-stable routing result would be truthful only on first execution and then revert to stable defaults on inspect/replay. The native outcome is now stored per transition and non-stable first-call, replay, and inspection behavior is covered.

Review found that the existing Full Harness trust copy explicitly denied Minecraft authority while the new bootstrap used it for Minecraft application lifecycle. The UI now separately discloses installed local environment application start/stop authority and continues to deny every in-environment action and answer/terminal authority.

The work packet incorrectly called a pre-tick screen_open cancellation manual interruption evidence. It is now classified only as UI-state safety cancellation; genuine manual input override remains required.

The exact bind control was resolved before smooth scrolling, but the outline retained its pre-scroll rectangle and appeared over the later profile-disconnect confirmation. Deterministic scrolling plus lifetime geometry tracking now keeps the outline attached to the exact element.

The profile OAuth readiness badge said Active binding even though it proved no chat-to-task relationship. It now says Active account link and explicitly directs the operator to the separate exact-task binding step.

The rebuilt server advertises nullable action_authority_id for trusted-device Minecraft lifecycle bootstrap, but this already-running Codex task's connector schema still requires a string and rejects null before the request reaches the server. The native stable-scope transition and tool-list-changed notification succeeded; one client catalog reconnection is still required to live-test the new schema.

remaining_acceptance: A complete environment.capacity_capture.v1 remains required: this journey did not emit every event-to-evidence, evidence-to-pickup, stop-to-replan, finalized-steering-to-stop, manual-or-safety-to-release, observation-byte/token/coalescing, lead-time, controlled_n0, and unknown_world measurement needed for environment.capacity_report.v1.

ET6 must not be promoted until the capacity reporter returns exit_satisfied=true; the exact binding, pickup/acknowledgement, Minecraft action/re-entry, manual override, reconnect, action revoke/stale rejection, reasoning revoke/stale pickup rejection, and normal shutdown lifecycle is accepted independently.
